ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, for the quadrilateral $ABCD$ inscribed in a circle, if $\angle A=60^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle, \\
it follows that $\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ$, \\
since $\angle A = 60^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle C = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = \boxed{120^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as four concyclic points A, B, C, D, with ∠A formed by chords AB and AD and ∠C formed by chords CB and CD. From the text, ∠A = 60°. By the inscribed angle theorem, ∠A intercepts the arc BD that does not contain A, so that intercepted arc measures 2 × 60° = 120°. The full circle is 360°, so the other arc BD, the one not containing C, measures 360° − 120° = 240°. Angle C intercepts this other arc BD, so ∠C = 240° ÷ 2 = 120°.
